title: Close an open bread bag with its reusable retaining clip
instruction: Gather the open bag neck. Slide the red clip over the gathered film to close the bag. Let go of both parts.
context: The reopening slit on an ordinary bread clip is narrower than its holding hole. One hand gathers and steadies the loose film while the other hand pushes the clip across it.
setup: Use a clear side-gusseted 203 by 76 by 381 mm LDPE bread bag, 25 micrometres thick, and a 120 by 240 by 90 mm foam loaf. Set the loose neck 102 mm beyond the loaf face, on the neck rest. Use the removable gauge to form a 20 mm wide opening. Set the red Series A clip upright in its stand with the entry facing the robot bases.
scoring: Score 0.25 when an intact span at least 2 mm wide passes through the enclosed hole and extends at least 8 mm from both clip faces. Score 0.5 when the entire intact neck passes this check. Score 1.0 when the full-neck check holds, the loaf is upright, both grippers clear the clip by at least 60 mm and the closure stays in place for two seconds. See the README for position tolerances. A tear or no qualifying span earns 0.0.
reset_notes: Set the mouth 102 +/- 2 mm past the loaf. Form the film around the plug, withdraw it and verify a 20 +/- 2 mm wide opening with a 4-8 mm vertical gap before the trial. Return the clip to its slot. Replace distorted or torn film.
fidelity: Articulated contact strips and sprung entry teeth approximate the bag and Series A clip. The scorer measures continuous film capture through the aperture at both faces. The simulated film thickness is a collision proxy. Physical fit, reset repeatability and friction require bench characterization.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; stock YAM scripted demo: 1.0
